disclosures: All three machines belong to one owner: the dual-evaluator integrity check ran under a single operator and shows the mechanism, not independence.
The pinned reference is the approximate circuit's output; the approximation differs from the float64 model on 2.5% of arbitrary three-letter prompts (plaintext audit).
Evaluation keys are reused across sessions until the requester's 24-hour epoch expiry; the requester's secret key is stored as a 0600 file for that period.
Prompts were chosen at run time and were not used in any earlier run or test.
No independent cryptographic review has taken place.

crossArchitectureCheck.note: Insecure development ring (N = 2^12), prompt bdf, two steps, before the proof.
crossArchitectureCheck.result: Both encoders gave byte-identical results across linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 here; the proof used the big-float encoder because float64 agreement is not guaranteed.
